groups.name: CsvEncodingBenchmarks
groups.description: Round-trips SampleRecords through CSV in UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32 to show the encoding's effect on (de)serialization cost. Export = serialize the typed rows to bytes in the encoding; Parse = read those bytes back into typed rows. UTF-8 is the baseline.

parameters.name: RowCount
parameters.description: Number of SampleRecord rows round-tripped (10,000 or 100,000).

dataset.notes: Flat 7-column record; only the byte encoding differs between algorithms.

measurements.description: Serialize the rows to UTF-8 CSV bytes (baseline encoding).
measurements.slaStandard: Encoding choice should not blow the CSV (de)serialization budget; round-trips of up to 100k rows should stay within a few hundred milliseconds regardless of encoding.

measurements.description: Serialize the rows to UTF-16 (little-endian) CSV bytes.
measurements.slaStandard: Encoding choice should not blow the CSV (de)serialization budget; round-trips of up to 100k rows should stay within a few hundred milliseconds regardless of encoding.

groups.name: CsvNestedBenchmarks
groups.description: Serializes and parses a NestedRecord whose Address reference member itself nests a Geo coordinate. The CSV writer flattens these nested objects into leaf columns, so this captures the round-trip cost and the data structure that a flat row count alone hides.

parameters.name: RowCount

dataset.notes: Record with a nested Address object that itself nests a Geo coordinate (nesting depth 2); the CSV writer flattens these into leaf columns.

measurements.description: Serialize the nested records to CSV bytes (writer flattens Address and Geo into columns).
measurements.slaStandard: Round-tripping up to 10k nested records through CSV should complete within a couple hundred milliseconds.

measurements.description: Parse the flattened CSV bytes back into typed NestedRecords (rebuilds the nested objects).
measurements.slaStandard: Round-tripping up to 10k nested records through CSV should complete within a couple hundred milliseconds.

groups.name: CsvReadBenchmarks
groups.description: Parses CSV (produced from RowCount SampleRecords) back through every read surface: buffered typed objects from bytes / stream / file, the IAsyncEnumerable streaming path, the async list path, the options-driven parse, and the dynamic DataTable and row/column-dictionary targets. Contrasts the peak-memory of materializing all rows against bounded streaming, and typed mapping against dynamic parsing.

name: csv
title: CSV
description: CSV write, read, split, and merge paths for Lyo.Csv over a flat 7-column SampleRecord (int/string/decimal/bool/DateTime). Covers typed object lists (bytes and string), streaming parse, DataTable round-trips, row-based split/combine (bytes and files), and multi-part merge. RowCount is the number of records; the data structure (columns and types) is captured in each class's data shape. The SampleRecord here is flat - nested objects/collections would add per-row flattening cost not represented by row count alone.
